title: Reginald Forsythe's arrangements and Deep Forest
summary: The band takes up collections to buy arrangements from Forsythe, who was in the country illegally and wrote Deep Forest first for Davison.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yes, but we had no job - you see - we were just rehearsing and I got Reginald Forsythe was arranging for Hines at that time---
Did Mort Croy also do some arrangements?
Yes, he did quite a few arrangements. I remember some of his arrangements were outstanding, but this guy was arranging for Earl Hines and he was - at this point - he was in the country illegally.

Yes. Reginald Forsythe. His visa had run out --------- he had no money either; none of us had any money; so, the guys in the band - we used to take up a collection and give him $35.00 for one of his big arrangements and I had a whole book full of his arrangements---
What ever happened to that stuff?
Oh, I had it for years and, finally, God - carrying it around is a pain - you know--

It just disappeared -- I gave it to other people - they were far - way ahead of themselves in arrangements, you know. And, actually, 'Deep Forest', which was Earl Hines' theme song, he really wrote that for me -- first --

Forsythe-- and then when Earl Hines heard it, he said -- gee, I got to have that for a theme song; that's beautiful and he took it -- well, why not -- what the hell. And, of course, this went on until finally - oh, lots of things in between but what really happened here was we got a job at Guyons Paradise Ballroom - our first job --
